thread:
maya: quick sync — prepping rollout checklist for cache crediting on the new cost dashboard. want to make sure telemetry + routing signals map to per-route and per-model unit economics. thoughts?
alex: high-level — we need three things: 1) deterministic token attribution, 2) storing cache hits as negative-cost events, 3) sampling logic for high-volume tenants. :memo:
sam: for deterministic attribution, i'd vote for a left-most match on route tags, then fallback to model SKU. avoids double-counting when routes share prompts. simplest to explain in docs.
maya: left-most match makes sense. how do we handle prefix cache hits that are shared? i.e., same prefix used by multiple routes but should credit the owner route.
jun: proposal — maintain a prefix->route lineage table populated at request-time when prefix is created. on cache hit, attribute to the route in lineage unless TTL expired. if multiple, pick most-recent. this keeps ownership stable.
alex: lineage table ok but expensive. instead consider periodic backfill: attribute cache credits by sampling 1% of requests and run offline lineage join. scale-wise cheaper but adds lag.
sam: offline sampling is nice for cost, but customers want near-real-time dashboards for anomaly alerts. can we do hybrid? realtime best-effort, then reconcile with batch.
maya: hybrid seems like the right UX tradeoff. show 'reconciled' vs 'live' numbers in UI. :eyes:
jun: also need to surface uncertainty. add `confidence` field to per-route cost rows: High/Medium/Low depending on sampling and lineage TTL.
alex: regarding telemetry payloads — add `route_id`, `model_sku`, `cache_hit` (bool), `cache_prefix_id` (opt), `token_count`, `response_latency_ms`. keep payload <1KB.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: cost-telemetry-v2 -> staging at 2026-03-19T22:00Z
maya: UX question — in the cost dashboard should we default to model-level grouping or route-level? product expects route-level first, but model-level is better for engineering breakdowns.
sam: default to route-level with a quick toggle to model-level. also remember per-token effective price column: tokens_charged - cache_credits / tokens_charged.
alex: adding SQL example for reconciler pipeline:
```sql
-- reconcile cached credits
WITH hits AS (
  SELECT cache_prefix_id, route_id, count(*) as hits
  FROM sampled_requests
  WHERE cache_hit = true
  GROUP BY cache_prefix_id, route_id
)
INSERT INTO cache_credits
SELECT h.route_id, sum(h.hits)*avg(token_count)*model_price
FROM hits h JOIN model_prices p ON p.model_sku = h.model_sku
GROUP BY h.route_id;
```
maya: nice. timeline: want staging test next week, then gradual rollout to prod with canary at 5% traffic. need runbook plus notification to billing and support.
jun: will add runbook drafts to the doc. 
alex: one more ask — expose per-tenant toggle to opt-out of live attribution if they want eventual reconciliation only.
maya: added. thanks team — i'll schedule a 30m sync to finalize the checklist. :rocket:
sam: +1
jun: +1
alex: thanks! :thumbsup:
